# Introducing Brooklyn

In this report, I will be telling you all about **Brooklyn the Basking shark** (*Cetorhinus maximus*), and her journey along the eastern shore of the United States of America. During her journey through the Atlantic Ocean, Brooklyn used her **gill rakers** to feed on phytoplankton and small crustaceans within the water column.

```{r load-packages, include = FALSE}
packages <- c("tidyverse", "sf", "rnaturalearth", "rnaturalearthdata")

# Install packages not yet installed
installed_packages <- packages %in% installed.packages()

if (any(installed_packages == FALSE)) {
  install.packages(packages[!installed_packages])
}

# Packages loading
invisible(lapply(packages, library, character.only = TRUE))
```

```{r load spatial-data, include = FALSE}
# Country polygons for the Americas
coast <- ne_countries(scale = "medium", returnclass = "sf")

# Ocean polygon
ocean <- ne_download(scale = "medium", 
                     type = "ocean", 
                     category = "physical",
                     returnclass = "sf")
```

```{r load-shark-data, include = FALSE}
# Download shark tracking data directly, ERDDAP servers often go down for maintenance, looks like that's currently the case 
sharks <- read.csv("https://erddap.bco-dmo.org/erddap/tabledap/bcodmo_dataset_476315.csv", 
                   skip = 1)  # Skip the units row

#We'll load the csv directly to be safe
#sharks <- read.csv("../Data/basking_sharks.csv")
sharks <- sharks[-1,]

# Clean column names
colnames(sharks) <- c("ptt", "tuid", "year", "month", "day", "longitude", "latitude", "date", "type", "depth_min", "temp_depth_min", "depth_max", "depth_range", "tsst")

# Convert date column and add month name
sharks <- sharks %>%
  mutate(
    across(c(ptt, tuid, year, month, day, longitude, latitude, 
             depth_min, temp_depth_min, depth_max, depth_range, tsst), as.numeric),
    date = as.Date(date, format = "%m/%d/%Y"),
    month_name = month.abb[month]
  )


# Convert to spatial object
sharks_sf <- st_as_sf(sharks, 
                      coords = c("longitude", "latitude"),
                      crs = 4326)
```

```{r summary-table, include = FALSE}
shark_summary <- sharks %>%
  group_by(ptt) %>%
  summarise(
    n_locations = n(),
    start_date = min(date, na.rm = TRUE),
    end_date = max(date, na.rm = TRUE),
    days_tracked = as.numeric(end_date - start_date),
    min_lat = min(latitude),
    max_lat = max(latitude)
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(days_tracked))

#kable turns a dataframe into a nicely formatted table, much better than the raw output of shark_summary
knitr::kable(shark_summary, 
             digits = 1)
## same as summary() but looks nicer, digits = 1 means that its rounding the numbers in the output
```

```{r filtering-my-shark, include = FALSE}
my_shark <- 88143

my_data <- sharks %>%
  filter(ptt == my_shark) %>%
  arrange(date)

my_sf <- sharks_sf %>%
  filter(ptt == my_shark) %>%
  arrange(date)


```

```{r, include = FALSE}
start_point <- my_data[1,]
end_point <- my_data[62,]
```

# Brooklyn's Journey

## Map of Brooklyn's journey

```{r, echo = FALSE}
# Edit the settings of this chunk to render appropriately, what do you need to add to {r}?


# Calculate map extent from this shark's data
bbox <- st_bbox(my_sf)
xlim <- c(bbox["xmin"] - 3, bbox["xmax"] + 3)
ylim <- c(bbox["ymin"] - 3, bbox["ymax"] + 3)

# Build the map layer by layer
ggplot() +
  # Layer 1: Ocean background
  geom_sf(data = ocean, fill = "lightblue1") +
  
  # Layer 2: Land polygons
  geom_sf(data = coast, fill = "palegreen4") +
  
  # Layer 3: Track line connecting points
  geom_path(data = my_data, aes(x = longitude, y = latitude, color = "black")) +
  
  # Layer 4: Points colored by month
  geom_point(data = my_data, aes(x = longitude, y = latitude, color = month_name)) +
  stat_sf_coordinates(geom = "point")+
  
  # Layer 5: Start point (green triangle)
  geom_point(data = start_point, aes(x= longitude, y = latitude), shape = 17, size = 2, color = "green") +
  
  # Layer 6: End point (red square)
  geom_point(data = end_point, aes(x= longitude, y = latitude), size = 2, color = "red" ) +
  
  # Set map extent
coord_sf(xlim = xlim, ylim = ylim, expand = FALSE) +
  scale_color_manual(
  name = "Month",
  values = c("Jan" = "#313695", "Feb" = "#4575b4", "Mar" = "#f46d43",
             "Apr" = "#fee090", "May" = "#d73027","Jul" = "#fdae61", 
             "Oct" = "#a50026", "Nov" = "#762a83", "Dec" = "#40004b")
  )+
  labs(
    title = paste("Migration of Brooklyn the Basking Shark"),
    x = "Longitude", y = "Latitude"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold"),
    legend.position = "right"
  )

```

# Post-Swim Review

After all that swimming, Brooklyn derserves to be recognized for her hard work! Here is the official **breakdown**

Drumroll please....

```{r, include = FALSE}
## The latitudinal change (difference between max and min latitude)
max_lat <- max(my_data$latitude)
min_lat <- min(my_data$latitude)
max_lat - min_lat 
max_depth <- max(my_data$depth_max, na.rm = TRUE)
## The total distance your shark traveled in km
## summed dif between every point 

library(units)
dist_m <- sum(st_distance(my_sf$geometry))
dist_km <- set_units(dist_m, km)
```

# Brooklyn's Journey Summary Stats

|                         |                     |
|-------------------------|---------------------|
| Starting Location       | (-70.2943, 42.0470) |
| Ending Location         | (-68.3400, 42.1050) |
| Latitudinal Change      | 12.7214             |
| Total Distance Traveled | 2692393km           |
| Maximum Depth           | 1080                |

**Wow!!!**
From Oct 11, 2008 to Oct 1, 2009, Brooklyn traveled over 2 million km! That is over 4 million times the height of the CN Tower. To fuel her mission, she likely had to eat a lot of phytoplankton. On average, basking sharks filter around 2000 tons of water each day, so over the course of Brooklyn's journey, she could have filtered over 710000 tons of water. 

**Great job Brooklyn!**
